name: Seedling Tray
tagline: 6-cup seed starter that feeds your Hydro Tower
summary: A 6-cup hydroponic seed starter. Fill the tray with water and nutrients, sow into the net cups and let the roots grow down into the water. The cups are the same as the Hydro Tower's, so seedlings move straight into the tower without touching the roots. Prints without supports.
caption:
From seed to tower. 🌱

Sow in the cups, add water, watch the roots grow.
When they're ready, move each cup straight into the Hydro Tower.
No soil. No mess. Zero supports.

print.material: PETG (holds water for weeks); PLA is fine for the lid and cups
print.orientation: Tray upright; lid flat with the wide side of the holes up; cups standing
print.bed: No brim needed; tray uses 192 × 130 mm of bed
notes: For a fully watertight tray print 4 walls and 5 bottom layers
Keep the water 1–2 cm below the cups once roots appear
Use rockwool cubes or clay pebbles inside the cups

steps: Print the tray, the lid and 6 net cups.
Fill the tray with water and nutrients up to the top mark.
Drop the lid onto the ledge and put a cup in each hole.
Put a rockwool cube in each cup and sow 2–3 seeds per cube.
When roots come out of the cups, lower the water to the lower mark.
After 2–3 weeks, lift each cup out and drop it straight into the Hydro Tower.

name: Hydro Tower
summary: A vertical hydroponic tower you can stack as high as you like. Each segment has three 45° pockets for standard net cups and twists 60° from the one below, so every plant gets light. A small pump lifts water to the top cap, it trickles down through the roots and drains back into the bucket through the base. Prints without supports.
caption:
Grow up, not out. 🌱

A hydroponic tower you can print at home.
6 plants. 20 cm wide. Zero supports.
Want more? Just stack another level.

print.material: PETG (water resistant) — avoid PLA for parts that sit in water for months
print.orientation: Segments upright with the spigot on the bed; cap flat, inlet up
print.bed: Brim 5 mm on segments for tall stacks of prints
notes: Print one segment per level and 3 net cups per segment
Use an opaque bucket as reservoir and a 3–5 W aquarium pump
Paint or print in white to keep algae away

you_need: Opaque bucket with lid, 10–20 L (the water reservoir)
Aquarium tubing up to 10 mm outer Ø, about 1 m (tower height + 30 cm)
Clay pebbles or rockwool cubes to hold the seedlings
Optional: plug-in timer (15 min on / 45 min off)
steps: Print 1 base, 2 segments, 6 net cups and 1 top cap. PETG, no supports.
Cut an 80–100 mm hole in the centre of the bucket lid and sit the base over it.
Drop the pump to the bottom of the bucket and run the tubing straight up through the base.
Push the first segment's spigot into the base socket. Stack the next one twisted 60° so the pockets don't line up.
Feed the tubing up through the segments into the top cap inlet, then press the cap on.
Fill the bucket with water and nutrients, keeping the level below the base.
Put seedlings in clay pebbles inside the net cups and drop one into each pocket.
Switch the pump on: water rises to the cap and trickles back down through the roots.
